h1: The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 — Pool, Buffet Breakfast in Bangkok's Favourite Street-Food Hood
intro: Chokchai 4 is one of Bangkok's most beloved late-night eating streets — noodle joints, grilled seafood, fried everything, all humming until 2 AM — and The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 sits right in the middle of it. This 4-star hotel offers what few Bangkok properties at this price point deliver together: an outdoor swimming pool, a generous breakfast buffet, a free gym, and free parking, in a neighbourhood that feels genuinely local rather than tourist-packaged. 174 rooms from approximately ฿600/night, rated 7.9 out of 10 from 1,206 reviews on Trip.com — solid numbers that reflect a hotel which punches above its price class, with a few honest caveats worth knowing before you book.

body.html: Who is this hotel for? In short: The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 is built for mid-budget travellers who want a pool and a real breakfast without paying five-star rates. The guest mix reflects this perfectly — Thai families visiting Bangkok for errands or events, business travellers from upcountry who need free parking and a decent night's sleep, Chinese tourists who appreciate the bilingual (Chinese-speaking) front-desk team and the generous buffet spread, and couples or friend groups who want a pool without retreating to a Sukhumvit luxury tower.

Location and getting around — The hotel sits at 519 Chok Chai 4 Soi 60, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230, on the northeast corridor of Thanon Lat Phrao, roughly 3 km from the Ha Yaek Lat Phrao interchange. This is a real residential neighbourhood, not a tourist bubble: 7-Elevens, fresh markets, local noodle shops and the legendary Chokchai 4 street-food strip are all within walking distance. For reaching the wider city: Grab and taxis are reliable from the soi entrance. Central Plaza Ladprao and Union Mall (Ha Yaek) are about 7 minutes by car. The MRT Blue Line at Phahon Yothin connects to the inner city, though you'll need a taxi or Grab to bridge the gap from the hotel. If you're driving, the free on-site parking is one of the best reasons to choose this hotel.

"Room was spacious with a balcony overlooking the pool. Breakfast buffet had so many choices — Thai and Western. Paid less than ฿700 per night including breakfast for two. Didn't expect this quality at this price."

Rooms — The 174 air-conditioned rooms span Deluxe King, Deluxe Twin, Superior Twin and Deluxe King Garden View categories. Every room comes with a private balcony — a genuine selling point that reviewers consistently call out — plus a mini-bar, flat-screen TV with satellite channels, fridge, kettle, rainfall shower and complimentary toiletries. Room sizes are comfortable without being cavernous. The honest caveat, drawn from real reviews: the building is showing its age in places. Some guests mention worn bathroom fixtures, ageing ceiling panels or noisier air-conditioning units. That said, the overwhelming majority describe rooms as clean and functional for the price — which is ultimately what matters here.

Swimming pool and fitness — The outdoor pool is a genuine highlight. Reviewers describe it as clean, well-maintained and a comfortable size for leisurely laps or just floating around. It's not a resort-scale infinity pool, but it's perfectly enjoyable and not something you'd typically find at this price in Bangkok's Lat Phrao corridor. The gym is free for guests and covers the basics, and there's a massage room on-site for when your muscles disagree with the traffic. The lobby itself is fairly compact — don't expect the grand-foyer feel of a Silom business hotel.

Breakfast buffet — the most-praised feature — The buffet runs daily from 6:00 to 10:00 AM, and it's the element guests mention most in reviews. The spread is legitimately wide: Thai staples (congee, rice porridge, stir-fries, fried items) alongside Western options (eggs cooked to order, bread, cake, fresh fruit). Multiple reviews flag this as a genuine value-add, with guests remarking they couldn't believe two people's breakfast was included at this nightly rate. A few reviews note dishes can run low during peak times, which is fairly standard for a property this size. Always confirm at booking whether breakfast is included in your rate.

Service and staff — Across 1,206 Trip.com reviews (7.9/10) and the Booking.com breakdown (staff score: 7.6, which is the hotel's highest individual category), the picture is clear: the team at the front desk is consistently praised for being friendly, helpful and patient. Staff assist with taxi bookings, recommend restaurants in the soi, and notably handle Chinese-speaking guests with ease. The most common complaint in reviews is the Wi-Fi connectivity — weak signal in certain rooms and floors. If you need reliable internet for remote work or video calls, bring a Thai SIM or pocket Wi-Fi as backup.

Price and value — Deluxe rooms typically run from approximately ฿600–800/night in low season. Factor in a breakfast-inclusive package for two and the price-per-night becomes remarkably competitive for a hotel with a pool. High-season or long-weekend rates can push to ฿900–1,200. Booking.com's guest value-for-money score of 7.3 — notably higher than the overall score — tells you that guests consistently feel they get more than they paid for. Compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before committing, as prices vary platform to platform.

Honest verdict — From 1,206 Trip.com reviews (7.9) and broader platform data, The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 emerges as the most value-driven pool-and-breakfast hotel in the Lat Phrao corridor. The breakfast buffet is a genuine draw, the pool is well-kept, and the staff make up for whatever the ageing building lacks. The real limitations — weak Wi-Fi, signs of wear in some rooms, car-dependent location — are worth knowing upfront but don't undermine the core offer. If you want a pool, a hot breakfast, and a window into Bangkok's lived-in northeast rather than its tourist centre, this hotel delivers exactly that.

highlights.title: Outdoor Pool + Free Gym
highlights.text: Clean outdoor pool and a complimentary gym — amenities that few Bangkok hotels at this price point offer together. Massage room also available on-site.

highlights.title: Generous Breakfast Buffet · Thai + Western
highlights.text: Daily buffet from 6–10 AM with a wide Thai and Western spread. Consistently the top-mentioned positive in guest reviews — excellent value when included in the room rate.

highlights.title: Chokchai 4 Street Food — Open Till 2 AM
highlights.text: Bangkok's favourite late-night food soi is steps from the door. Noodles, grilled seafood, fried snacks and fresh market stalls — real local eating, not a tourist strip.

honestSummary: The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 is the most value-packed pool-and-breakfast hotel in Lat Phrao — the buffet is a genuine highlight, rooms have private balconies, and staff are friendly. The building is ageing, Wi-Fi is patchy, and you need wheels to explore the city. Not a glamorous property, but it delivers honestly on what it promises.

tips.title: Walk Chokchai 4 at Night
tips.body: The street-food strip on Soi Chokchai 4 runs until after midnight — grilled meats, seafood, noodle soups and fried snacks. It's a short walk or motorbike-taxi hop from the hotel entrance. Don't skip it.

tips.title: Hit the Pool Before 9 AM
tips.body: The pool is quietest in the early morning before 9:00 AM. Swim first, then head up to the breakfast buffet before it closes at 10:00 AM — the ideal morning routine here.

tips.title: Carry a Thai SIM for Internet
tips.body: Hotel Wi-Fi is frequently cited as weak and unreliable. Pick up a prepaid AIS, DTAC or TRUE SIM at the airport or a 7-Eleven if you need solid connectivity for work or navigation.

tips.title: Free Parking — Drive In Confidently
tips.body: Free on-site parking accommodates sedans and vans comfortably. If you're road-tripping from a province or driving in from suburban Bangkok, this is one of the hotel's strongest practical advantages.

faqTitle: FAQ — The President Hotel at Chokchai 4

faq.q: Where is The President Hotel at Chokchai 4 located?
faq.a: The hotel is at 519 Chok Chai 4 Soi 60, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230. It sits on the northeast stretch of Thanon Lat Phrao, about 7 minutes by car from Central Plaza Ladprao and Union Mall (Ha Yaek Lat Phrao). Grab and taxis reach the city centre in 30–45 minutes depending on traffic.

faq.q: What is the room rate at The President Hotel at Chokchai 4?
faq.a: Deluxe rooms start from approximately ฿600–800/night in the low season. Packages including buffet breakfast for two push the value further. High-season or long-weekend rates can rise to ฿900–1,200. Compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com — prices vary by platform.

faq.q: Does the hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — one outdoor pool, free for all guests. Reviews consistently describe it as clean and well-maintained. It's a comfortable leisure size, not a lap-swimming pool. The hotel also offers a free gym and on-site massage room.

faq.q: How good is the breakfast buffet?
faq.a: It runs daily from 06:00 to 10:00 AM and is the most praised feature in guest reviews. The spread covers Thai staples (congee, stir-fries, fried items) and Western options (cooked-to-order eggs, bread, cake, fresh fruit). Confirm at booking whether your rate includes breakfast.

Wi-Fi is free but inconsistent — multiple reviews flag weak signal in certain rooms and floors. If you need dependable connectivity for remote work, video calls or streaming, bring a Thai SIM card (AIS/DTAC/TRUE) or a pocket Wi-Fi device.

faq.q: Is there free parking at the hotel?
faq.a: Yes, free on-site parking is available. It comfortably accommodates sedans and vans — one of the strongest practical reasons to choose this hotel for travellers arriving by car from outside Bangkok.
